title: Confidence Census
tagline: A table-lint that counts what the fourteen reference tables actually say about themselves, and reports the gaps the embed test cannot see.
pitch: A command-line linter (`census.mjs <tables-dir>`) that walks `data/tables/*.json` and emits a findings JSON plus a phone-friendly report page. Per table it produces the certain/likely/recall census and reconciles it against the policy column `data/README.md` states by hand; lists rows with no `source`; rows whose `source` text says 'recall' or 'from memory' while the label is `likely` or `certain` (a review list, not a defect list: stock has 44, drills 16, fasteners_un 12, npt 7, materials_thermal 7, avionics 3 at 0974a62); every `disputed` entry as a browsable ledger (airframes 169, motors 53, stock 48, drills 10, rails 10, orings 9, avionics 8, motor_perf 7); row fields the table's `columns` block never describes (airframes `lengths_all_mm`/`pns_all`, motor_perf `disputed`, and ten fields of `design_factors_nasa` including `ultimate_design_factor`); tables with no date anywhere in their metadata (9 of 14: airframes, avionics, drills, fasteners_metric, fits, materials_thermal, motor_perf, npt, stock — the roadmap's guard asks for a data-date on every hint line); supplements' own census (motors supplement 30 recall of 119, airframes supplement 25 of 48); inch↔mm pairs that disagree beyond the rounding the `columns` text declares; and mode-vs-median length outliers in motors (Loki|38/240 stores 117 mm against variants 177/177.8/190; AMW 75-3500 497 against 870). The maintainer opens the page, filters by severity (defect / review / info) and table, and reads each finding with the row key.
whyNow: docs/roadmap-evaluation.md 'The five to build first' item 2 (the data-integrity sweep, 'wrong numbers shipping right now') and 'Wrong-number risks' #2 guard ('a data-date on every hint line'); data/README.md confidence-policy table (hand-written, nothing reconciles it); tests/flight-db.test.mjs '== data integrity ==' covers only ID<OD, walls, vocabulary and duplicates.
computes: Inputs: the 14 table files (or the committed excerpt). Logic: per-row invariants (key present and unique; confidence ∈ {certain,likely,recall}; source non-empty; label-vs-source-text; field_confidence stricter than row confidence), per-table invariants (every row field documented in `columns`; a date in reconciliation/notes/columns; license_note present), numeric sanity (in×25.4 vs mm within the declared rounding; motors len_mm vs median of len_variants ±20%), and a census compared with the counts parsed from data/README.md's policy column. Outputs: findings.json [{table,key,rule,severity,detail}], a Markdown summary, exit 1 on any 'defect', and a report page that renders findings.json with filters.
dataNeeded: tools/snapshot.mjs excerpts of the ten small tables (key, confidence, disputed, field_confidence, source: ≈80 KB) and key+confidence only for drills and motor_perf (≈40 KB); the CLI is run once against /home/user/Partforge and its findings.json (≈30 KB) is committed with a --sidecar-only provenance record naming data/tables at 0974a62; data/README.md snapshot (12 KB) for the policy reconciliation. ≈ 170 KB total.
existingOverlap: tests/flight-db.test.mjs checks resolver behaviour and a handful of row invariants; tests/flight-db-embed.test.mjs proves the embedded literal equals the files row by row. Neither censuses confidence, checks documentation of fields, dates, label-vs-text, supplements or outliers, and the README policy column is reconciled by nobody. This reports; it never edits a table.
honestyRisks: Label-vs-text hits are deliberate in places (PROVENANCE.md names stock's 44 likely rows as corroborated), so the rule must class them 'review' and quote the source text; parsing the README policy prose can mis-count, so the parser is pinned by tests to the current README and a parse failure is reported as 'could not reconcile', never as a defect; the inch↔mm check must read each field's declared rounding from `columns` (orings tolerances are stored to 0.01 mm against 3-dp IDs — 339 pairs differ only by that) or report 'info'; the page shows the committed findings and says the commit they were read at, so a stale page cannot pass for a fresh run.
testPlan: node --test: each rule fires on a planted fixture (missing source, 'recall' text under 'certain', an undocumented field, a duplicate key, a 117-vs-177 length) and is silent on a clean one; against the snapshot: drills 204 certain / 74 likely / 4 recall, airframes 161 recall, stock 148 recall, motor_perf 162 recall, avionics 19 recall (the README's own numbers), exactly 9 tables flagged dateless, design_factors_nasa's undocumented-field list contains `ultimate_design_factor`, both motor outliers named; a fresh run equals the committed findings.json byte for byte; tools/smoke.mjs at 1280 and 390 px.
landing: PartForge tools/db/lint.mjs run from tests/run.mjs after the embed test; the report as docs/data/census.html or a section of ⚙ Settings → Data sources; the README policy table generated from the census instead of typed. To ship: thresholds and severities agreed in data/README.md, and the 'review' class triaged once by the maintainer so the exit code can be made strict.
notes: Build-first item 2; verified data/README.md's hand-written policy column and that flight-db tests check only a few row invariants. Undocumented fields, dateless tables and motor length outliers are concrete findings.

Verified design_factors_nasa has undocumented row fields including ultimate_design_factor and the README's hand-written policy prose; counts are claimed from a session run and classed review-not-defect, which is the right posture.

stock.json shows recall 148 / likely 44 as pitched; the 14 tables share the {table, license_note, columns, rows, notes, reconciliation} shape. Many rules and a README-policy parser make it a full medium build; the 'review' class for label-vs-text hits is the right honesty move.
